newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close higher ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close higher ahead of CPI.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Thursday with exception of dollar-linked bonds ahead of the publication of April's consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 to 105.2
Volume including Makams was 120 million shekels.
"There was demand for all kinds of bonds," said an investment manager at one of the big banks.
He said that on a typical CPI day it was uncharacteristic to see rises both in CPI-linked bonds and in unlinked bonds.

"The rises in both are because there were very different opinions in the market about the CPI. The optimists believed the CPI would rise a low 0.8 percent, while pessimists forecast a high 1.4 percent," he said. "So the optimists bought unlinked bonds and the pessimists the linked bonds."

The April CPI rise of 0.7 percent which was published after the close of the trading day was well below analysts' forecasts of about 1.1 percent and marked a comparative slowing of inflation from February and March.

"Demand today was up for all bonds but mostly for unlinked bonds because people expected the CPI to be low. This means a lower inflation and a possible cut in interest rates," said Ilan Doron at Solid Financial Markets.
"Demand for CPI-linked bonds was up because supply is low," he said. "Redemptions are higher than bond issues."
He said that prices of dollar-linked bonds were lower on the weaker dollar worldwide and in Israel.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3920 shekels against 3.3990 on Wednesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
